sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page bomk1234 (Bom-Kim); Childs 2025 p. 8 gives Bom = bomk1234/bmf and Kim (Krim) = krim1238/krm
sources.note: Identity only: alternative names Bom, Bome, Bomo, Bum; classification Mel > Bullom > Northern; refs Pichl 1972, Childs 2012; status nearly extinct.

sources.citation: Childs, G. Tucker. 2025. A grammar of Sherbro. Berlin: Language Science Press (LangSci 403), 582 pp. CC BY. DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15045985
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Describes Sherbro (sher1258), not Bom-Kim. Ch. 2 Phonology has 2.2 Tone (p. 41-43) and 2.3 Syllable structure but no word-stress section; the only 'stress' mentions are about Pichl's 1967 Sherbro dictionary notation ('5 levels of tone along with 5 levels of stress', p. 190). On Bom-Kim it says only: 'Both lexical and grammatical tone are found in other Bolom-Kisi languages that are still vital (Mani and Kisi), though tone is less prominent in the most moribund Bolom language Bom-Kim' (p. 41, PDF p. 67).
